miniProject.title: Portability audit with a clean reproduction and a losing regime
miniProject.brief: Close kernellab as defensible engineering on the RTX 3050: a per-kernel peak table with named clocks, an AMD dispatch defense, a three-branch fallback gate, scenario discipline, a repaired misleading benchmark, a read-only KernelBench and SOL check, one reconstructed production path with a bounded change, a clean rebuild and a workload-weighted report that keeps a loss.
steps: Build a per-kernel peak-bound table that names its clock: fp32 \(18 \times 128 \times 2 \times f\) gives \(6.8 \times 10^{12}\) at the 1470 MHz reference boost and \(9.7 \times 10^{12}\) at the 2100 MHz maximum reported by `nvidia-smi -q -d CLOCK` on the RTX 3050 6 GB, with 168 GB/s from \(12 \times 14 \times 10^9\) on the 96-bit bus for ridge points near 40 and 58 FLOP/byte. Place each kernel behind its Milestone E regime prediction with the falsifier that would reject it.

Write the dispatch and fallback defense so each dispatched path names its AMD CDNA and HIP counterpart with one-line roles, then implement the capability query plus dispatch with three tested branches on `sm_86`: native path when the feature query passes, portable fallback when forced off with correct results, and an explicit error when forced below the portable minimum.

Fix the stack for the full shape matrix, report timing boundaries, baseline precision and flags, input distributions, held-out status and workload frequency per shape. Audit a deliberately misleading benchmark with the five-line check (timing boundary, baseline parity, distributions, held-out status, cherry-picking) and correct every flaw, including TF32 parity: the audit must show matched precision before any speedup is kept. Sketch the Endpoints curve axes with point-count and duration rules and the fluidity deadline \(D_{i} = D_{p} + i \times D_{d}\) with its reset rule.

Run one KernelBench Level 1 problem with `scripts/run_and_check.py` usage 2 at commit 423217d with `gpu_arch` set to `Ampere` for capability 8.6, starting from the example kernels in `src/kernelbench/prompts`, then add one negated test that a reward-hacked kernel fails. Write the KernelBench contract from memory (levels, trials, `fast_p`, the four hidden distributions with scales, the ReLU-hack mechanism with its catching test). Derive the SOL-ExecBench RMSNorm speed-of-light bound by hand for one workload row with operations and bytes over peaks, compute its SOL-score from a measured time, list the four held-out axes with what each would break, and state which SOLAR assumptions cannot be reproduced without a B200 as read-only.

Trace one Milestone C kernel through graph, IR, kernel, dispatch and profile with bytes, launches and resources at each link. Write one bounded change with a predeclared mechanism hypothesis and the profiler signal that would falsify it, then test it on unseen shapes with correctness gates held.

Regenerate the full shape matrix from a clean checkout with a locked environment, raw samples and claim-to-artifact links for every table entry. Exercise all five protections, each with an injected-defect test that the protection catches (for example an unsupported dtype reaching the fast path, a tuned shape leaking into the held-out set, or a changed register allocation slipping past the version pin).

Compute the end-to-end bound for two share and speedup pairs, build the workload-weighted table with one losing row kept, and write the three-question defense: a stronger baseline that could overturn the claim, an alternate explanation for the gain, and the maintenance cost of keeping the path. State the dispatch and fallback choice per kernel family from the clean reproduction.
deliverables: The peak-bound table with named clocks and ridge points beside Milestone E predictions, and the AMD dispatch defense with the three-branch fallback tests.
The scenario-fixed shape matrix with boundaries and frequency, the five-line audit with the repaired misleading benchmark, and the KernelBench plus SOL hand-bound notes.

The reconstructed production path with its bounded change, the clean-build regeneration with claim links and five protection tests, and the workload-weighted report with a losing row and the three-question defense.

rubric.pass: Peaks name clocks with the ridge derived, each dispatched path names its AMD counterpart, and all three fallback branches are tested with correct results or the explicit error.
rubric.strong: The table states which Hopper and Blackwell features remain static audit.

rubric.pass: The shape matrix fixes the stack with boundaries and frequency stated, the misleading benchmark is repaired on all five lines with TF32 parity shown, and KernelBench and SOL limits are stated as read-only where hardware blocks execution.
rubric.strong: Held-out shapes and values are named with what each would break.

rubric.pass: The clean checkout regenerates tables with raw samples and claim links, each protection has an injected-defect test, and the weighted report keeps a losing row with the three-question defense.
rubric.strong: The per-family dispatch choice names its maintenance cost.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone defense: the peak table, audit, reconstruction, clean reproduction and weighted report with the losing regime are the final evidence package.
